- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk aversion or panic selling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative, model fails to adjust; apply mean reversion to forecast, pulling toward 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment >0.5, use 70% recent + 30% historical; if sentiment <0.3, use 30% recent + 70% historical.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3–5% gap), model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days if sentiment remains low.
- If true outcome is consistently above forecast, model may be underestimating sentiment impact; increase forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is rising or stable.
